messages:
maya: Quick sync — I ran the phasewise token-budget annealing experiment on canary dusk nodes. Goal: reduce KV thrash and give kernel selector clearer signals when prefill vs decode batches should be split. Results are mixed.
liam: TL;DR numbers? :eyes:
rachel: was this the annealing schedule that shrinks prefill budget over time? reminds me of the early warmup patch
maya: Yup. Schedule: start prefill_budget=96 tokens, anneal to 32 over 8s for long-lived streams. Decode_budget held at 16. Also added a small KV-probing heuristic: if KV hit rate < 30% in first 3 requests, temporarily cap prefill to 48 to avoid cold-path spilling.
oliver: Interesting. What did p50/p95 look like for short (<=64 token) requests?
maya: For short requests on the canary set:
- baseline (no anneal): p50=18ms p95=45ms
- anneal+kv-probe: p50=17ms p95=48ms
so p95 regressed ~6-7% for short flows. For long flows (>512 tokens) we saw tail improvement: p95 down ~9% and throughput up ~12% (better kernel packing).
sven: That aligns with kernel selector biasing toward dense kernels for longer prefill windows. The short-tail regression worries me.
liam: Do we have flame graphs or profiler traces? Kernel mismatch sounds like an extra memcpy or small-kernel fallback.
maya: Attached minimal profile snippet (excerpt):
```
[perf] hottest: attention_fused_dense_kernel (48%)
[perf] fallback: small_attention_dispatch (18%)
[memcpy] kv-span-copy (6%)
[sys] cuda-sync stalls (7%)
```
rachel: kv-span-copy at 6% suggests more frequent KV cache drains for short prefill bursts. Maybe annealing triggers earlier KV eviction.
oliver: Can you paste the config we used? I want to repro locally.
maya: Config we rolled to canary (yaml snippet):
```
batching:
  prefill_budget_initial: 96
  prefill_budget_min: 32
  anneal_seconds: 8
  decode_budget: 16
  kv_probe_window: 3
  kv_probe_threshold: 0.3
queue:
  prefill_batch_cap: 128
  decode_batch_cap: 64
```
liam: run this locally to reproduce: `./tools/bench_local --suite=short-prefill --nodes=2 --canary-config=anneal.yaml` ; I added a helper to emit per-request kv-hit stats.
eng-bot: Canary run summary uploaded: s3://redwood-canary/3951234567/summary.json (6:42am UTC)
rachel: I launched the local bench, seeing similar p95 bump. Also noticed decode latency variance reduced a lot (less oscillation).
sven: Hypothesis: annealing allows larger prefill batches early which improves throughput but creates sporadic KV churn that affects short requests on the same device. The kv_probe helps but the threshold needs tuning.
oliver: Two quick mitigations: (1) lower initial prefill_budget to 80 or 72, (2) reduce prefill_batch_cap to limit single-batch prefill size. Both should reduce KV churn without killing long-flow gains.
liam: I'd prefer dynamic cap: if node load > 70% or recent KV-hit-rate < 40% then cap prefill_batch_size down to 64. That keeps benefits only when node is healthy.
maya: Good plan. I'll try both: anneal_start=80 + dynamic cap rule. Also enabling a short KV-warmup grace window of 500ms where we bias toward smaller prefill to prime caches.
rachel: Can we add a quick golden test? Run the short-request suite (<=64) and long-request suite (>512) and assert p95 short not exceed baseline by >3% while long p95 improves >5%.
maya: Yup will add to CI. Plan for next steps:
1) implement dynamic prefill cap (liam rule) + reduce initial budget to 80
2) add 500ms kv-warmup bias
3) run canary and local benches, collect flame graphs
4) if short p95 stays within 3% of baseline, promote; else, roll back annealing and re-evaluate.
I'll push a PR with the config toggles and bench scripts this afternoon.
liam: add a conservatism flag we can flip via feature flag for Dedicated clusters.
oliver: cc @sre on rollout notes — we might see transient storage I/O for KV traces.
sven: thanks — ping me when PR is up, I can help with tracing and kernel selector logs.
maya: thanks all :thumbsup: will follow up with PR and results here.
